subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should the Browser upload tool keep the documented arm-then-click contract, or should managed profiles move toward an atomic upload-plus-trigger path as the preferred/default fix for this issue?
rationale: Current main has multiple plausible paths: documented arming, existing optional ref/inputRef/element atomic helpers, partial dispatcher-error fixes, and an unmerged timeout PR. Automation cannot safely choose the permanent Browser API semantics or compatibility tradeoff without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define atomic managed upload semantics
options.body: Keep this issue open to specify and prove an upload path that arms and triggers in one request, updates agent/CLI guidance, and covers dynamic-page stale refs.

options.title: Preserve arming as the contract
options.body: Treat paths-only upload arming as intentional, document the supported ref/inputRef/element alternatives more clearly, and leave only diagnostics or docs as follow-up.

options.title: Wait for live repro before design
options.body: Keep the issue in live-repro state until a reproducible dynamic-page fixture confirms the remaining timeout or stale-ref failure on current main.

recommendation.title: Define atomic managed upload semantics
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open to specify and prove an upload path that arms and triggers in one request, updates agent/CLI guidance, and covers dynamic-page stale refs.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser upload, dispatcher, and plugin-ownership history points most strongly to Peter Steinberger for the API/product boundary decision.
